query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a nanocrystalline structure in refractory high-entropy alloys through high-pressure torsion will improve their high-temperature mechanical capability by 15% while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance, due to the enhanced grain boundary strengthening mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloys in a coarse-grained state
generation.intervention: High-pressure torsion to introduce a nanocrystalline structure
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the high-temperature mechanical properties of nanocrystalline and coarse-grained refractory high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nanocrystalline alloy shows less than 10% improvement in high-temperature mechanical capability compared to the coarse-grained alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Since the inception of the concept of HEAs, numerous studies have been conducted to characterize their mechanical properties and microstructure evolution, chiefly of coarse-grained HEAs. Recently, efforts to study ultrafine-grained (UFG) HEAs produced by severe plastic deformation (SPD) have been undertaken. HEAs with nano or sub micron-grained structure have been shown to result in excellent mechanical properties,. In addition, since more conventional, coarse-grained HEAs exhibit a good combination of high strength and high fracture toughness at low temperatures,, an even better property profile can be expected of HEAs processed by SPD at cryogenic temperatures. High-pressure torsion (HPT) is one of the most popular SPD techniques as it is very efficient in reducing the grain size through a combination of high pressure and giant shear strain. Previously, nanocrystalline states were produced in a single phase CoCrFeMnNi HEA using HPT at ambient temperature. It was shown by tensile testing that a transition to a nanocrystalline structure gives rise to a significant increase of the room temperature strength accompanied with moderate ductility.
